**Finding submitted: Deviation (medium severity)**

**What I found:** The governing-law provision sits at § 20(h) (paragraph p0146), not in the main body of the general matters section where the planner first pointed. It selects **Nova Scotia law** (plus Canadian federal law applicable there) with the **non-exclusive jurisdiction of the Nova Scotia courts**.

**Why it deviates:** Nova Scotia falls outside the playbook's accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales). It is also not our home jurisdiction — Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited gains nothing here, so this is not an obligation benefiting our side that should be left alone.

**Mitigating factors I confirmed:**
- I searched for "arbitration" across the document and found only an incidental reference to arbitration fees inside the indemnity cost list (p0090) — there is **no mandatory arbitration clause and no foreign seat**, so this does not reach the walk-away threshold.
- The forum is already courts rather than arbitration, so only the jurisdiction words and forum required changing, consistent with the redline guidance.

**The redline** (validated `ok:true`) makes a surgical substitution, preserving the sentence structure:
- "laws of ~~Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia~~ **the State of New York**"
- "the ~~non-~~exclusive jurisdiction of the ~~courts of Nova Scotia~~ **state and federal courts located in New York County, New York**"

Note that I also tightened venue from non-exclusive to **exclusive**, matching the preferred position; non-exclusive jurisdiction would leave us exposed to being sued in multiple forums. The comment offers the Delaware/California/England-and-Wales fallback in case the counterparty resists New York, since Garman Routing Systems is US-based and may have its own preference within the accepted set.
